singlePurpose: BrowserCrew lets users run user-approved AI-assisted tasks on browser pages they choose, using AI services they configure, while keeping page access and browser actions under explicit user control.

listing.name: BrowserCrew
listing.shortDescription: Run user-approved AI tasks on the browser pages you choose, using cloud or local models you configure.

manifestPermissions.name: sidePanel
manifestPermissions.justification: Shows BrowserCrew's persistent task workspace beside the page the user is working on.
manifestPermissions.boundary: The panel opens only when the user invokes BrowserCrew.

manifestPermissions.name: storage
manifestPermissions.justification: Stores non-secret connection settings, task state, history, and machine-verifiable evidence in the extension profile; provider credentials use session storage instead of durable local storage.
manifestPermissions.boundary: BrowserCrew does not use storage permission to access website cookies or arbitrary browser data.

manifestPermissions.name: activeTab
manifestPermissions.justification: Lets BrowserCrew bind a task to the page the user is currently viewing before requesting any additional site access.
manifestPermissions.boundary: It does not authorize unrelated tabs or background browsing.

manifestPermissions.name: scripting
manifestPermissions.justification: Reads bounded visible-page observations and performs explicitly approved page actions required by the selected browser task.
manifestPermissions.boundary: Execution is limited by the selected-resource identity, site permission, workflow policy, stale-state checks, and approval checks.

manifestPermissions.name: tabs
manifestPermissions.justification: Reads selected-tab identity, title, and URL and detects navigation so BrowserCrew can reject stale or changed resources.
manifestPermissions.boundary: BrowserCrew does not use this permission to collect Chrome browsing history.

manifestPermissions.name: downloads
manifestPermissions.justification: Starts user-selected invoice downloads and verifies Chrome reports the intended file as complete before BrowserCrew reports success.
manifestPermissions.boundary: The bounded invoice workflow accepts only user-selected same-site invoice records and does not grant arbitrary filesystem reads.

optionalHostPermissions.justification: Allows BrowserCrew to request an exact HTTPS origin at runtime only when the user selects a website, AI endpoint, or MCP endpoint that requires access.
Allows runtime access to explicitly selected HTTP origins and local loopback AI/MCP services; BrowserCrew policy permits plain HTTP for local loopback AI and rejects unsafe cloud provider URLs.

categories.examples: Visible text, page title, page URL, supported form fields, selected record values, and invoice metadata from pages the user selects.
categories.purpose: Complete the browser task the user requested and verify its result.
categories.storage: Only bounded task/evidence data needed for local task history; hidden text, password fields, script text, and unselected-tab content are excluded by tested privacy boundaries.

categories.examples: Chat prompts, task instructions, and user-entered details supplied to BrowserCrew.
categories.purpose: Interpret and execute the user's requested AI-assisted browser task.
categories.storage: Task/history metadata can be stored locally when needed for the workflow; raw provider credentials are not stored here.

categories.examples: API credentials the user enters for a configured AI connection.
categories.purpose: Authenticate requests directly to the AI service selected by the user.
categories.storage: chrome.storage.session only; privacy tests require provider secrets to be absent from durable local storage and evidence artifacts.

categories.examples: Names, email addresses, phone numbers, or other details a user intentionally supplies for an approved form or attachment-backed task.
categories.purpose: Fill or reason about the user-requested task without inventing values.
categories.storage: Only when the selected workflow's local task/history needs the approved value; password fields are excluded.

categories.examples: Invoice records or financial details visible in user-selected invoice/document workflows.
categories.purpose: Identify and collect the exact invoices or documents the user selected.
categories.storage: Bounded local task/download metadata and user-requested exported manifest files.

categories.examples: BrowserCrew task status, approvals, recovery state, selected-resource identity, and completion evidence.
categories.purpose: Show progress/history, enforce approvals, recover safely, and prevent duplicate or stale actions.
categories.storage: Local extension storage and user-requested evidence/export files.

notCollectedForDeveloper: Chrome browsing history unrelated to a user-selected task
prohibitedUses: human review of user content by the BrowserCrew developer except when separately requested by the user for support and lawfully permitted

remoteCode.statement: BrowserCrew does not download or execute remote JavaScript or WebAssembly. AI and MCP responses are treated as data and remain behind BrowserCrew's local policy/tool boundaries.

requiredStoreAssets.spec: At least one 1280x800 or 640x400 product screenshot; BrowserCrew generates a real installed-extension 1280x800 Workspace screenshot
Optional/marketing video URL unless Dashboard requires it for the chosen listing flow

externalSubmissionRequirements: Chrome Web Store developer account with 2-step verification
Store listing fields completed in Developer Dashboard
Privacy practices fields completed and consistent with this contract and the public privacy policy
Reviewed public privacy-policy URL entered in Developer Dashboard
Reviewed public support URL entered in Developer Dashboard
